meta.name: Little Caesars
meta.disclaimer_extra: Little Caesars publishes its nutrition as a seven-page scanned flyer, not a data file, so these figures were read off pages 1 to 3 by hand. Every pizza figure is for a WHOLE pizza -- unlike Domino's and Papa John's, who publish per slice -- so divide by eight for one slice of a large. Topping figures are the chain's own note: "amounts shown are the highest count for each topping".
meta.blurb: Little Caesars is the one big pizza chain that still publishes nutrition as a scanned flyer, which is why almost nobody has put its numbers in a calculator. Its per-topping table adds onto a cheese base, so a Detroit-Style deep dish can be built topping by topping and then cut into the slices you actually eat.

categories.name: Pizza Base
categories.note: Every figure here is for a WHOLE pizza -- Little Caesars publishes per pizza, not per slice. They sell six crusts but publish a per-topping table for two, so those are the two you can build on; stuffed crust is here because they publish what adding it costs. Thin crust appears only as finished pizzas under menu items -- its toppings are not the round ones (their thin pepperoni is 150 calories over a thin cheese, against 350 on a round) -- and Crazy Crust and Stuffed Crazy Crust are on their menu but in neither the nutrition nor the ingredient pages of their guide.

categories.name: Toppings
categories.note: Little Caesars publishes the highest count for each topping, so a topping here is the most they put on. Building a pizza this way can come out above the same pizza on the menu -- base plus pepperoni lands exactly on the Classic Pepperoni, but base plus Italian sausage runs about 110 calories over it. Both figures are theirs.

ranch.reason: The flyer prints 32 g sugar against 4 g total carbohydrate for this dip, and sugar cannot exceed the carbohydrate it is part of. Buffalo Ranch -- the same dressing with hot sauce -- prints 3 g against the same 4 g of carbohydrate, so that is the figure used. Its 48 mg sodium is left exactly as printed: low for a dressing, but nothing in the row contradicts it.
